title: The Observatory Heist
summary: A priceless diamond is stolen during a thunderstorm at the Grand Observatory. Players must investigate the scene, interrogate suspects, and uncover the truth.

scenes.title: Observatory Main Hall
scenes.description: The main hall of the observatory, with a shattered glass display case that once held the Starfire Diamond. Rain pounds against the windows.

scenes.title: Director's Office
scenes.description: A cluttered office with books and papers. The observatory director, Dr. Aris, paces nervously.

scenes.title: Security Room
scenes.description: A small room with monitors showing camera feeds. The security guard, Mike, is reviewing footage.

scenes.title: Telescope Dome
scenes.description: The large dome housing the main telescope. A faint smell of ozone lingers.

characters.name: Dr. Elara Voss
characters.description: A brilliant but secretive astronomer who was working late.

characters.name: Mike Briggs
characters.description: The observatory's security guard, known for his strict adherence to protocol.

characters.name: Dr. Aris Thorne
characters.description: The observatory director, a meticulous man with a temper.

characters.name: Lena Park
characters.description: A quiet janitor who was cleaning the main hall before the heist.

characters.name: Detective Cole
characters.description: A seasoned detective who arrives to solve the case.

items.name: Broken glass shards
items.description: Shattered glass from the display case.
items.inspectText: The glass has a clean break, possibly cut with a glass cutter.

items.name: Muddy footprint
items.description: A footprint near the display case.
items.inspectText: The footprint is large, size 11, with a distinct tread pattern.

items.name: Wet umbrella
items.description: An umbrella in the director's office, still wet.
items.inspectText: The umbrella has a small tear and mud on the tip.

items.name: Security log
items.description: A log of entries for the night.
items.inspectText: The log shows a gap from 9:30 to 10:00 PM, when the guard was supposedly on patrol.

items.name: Burnt electrical wire
items.description: A short piece of wire with scorch marks.
items.inspectText: The wire appears to have been cut and then burnt with a lighter.

items.name: Leather glove
items.inspectText: The glove has a burn mark on the index finger, consistent with handling a hot wire.

clues.title: Glass cutter marks
clues.content: The glass was cut with a professional glass cutter, not broken by force.

clues.title: Shoe print match
clues.content: The footprint matches the shoes of Dr. Voss, who claimed she never left the lab.

clues.title: Umbrella mud
clues.content: The mud on the umbrella matches the soil from the garden outside the observatory, not the building interior.

clues.title: Log gap
clues.content: The security log has a 30-minute gap during which the alarm was disabled.

clues.title: Tampered alarm wire
clues.content: The burnt wire is from the alarm system, deliberately cut to disable it.

clues.title: Glove with burn
clues.content: The glove has a burn pattern matching the burnt wire, suggesting the wearer cut the wire.

dialogues.question: Where were you during the heist?
dialogues.answer: I was in my lab analyzing star charts. I didn't hear anything because of the thunder.

dialogues.question: Did you see anyone suspicious?
dialogues.answer: No, but I noticed Dr. Voss's shoes were muddy earlier. She claims she was inside all night.

dialogues.question: What were you doing at the time?
dialogues.answer: I was cleaning the main hall until about 9:30, then I took a break. The guard was in his room.

dialogues.question: What do you make of the burnt wire?
dialogues.answer: It's clear the alarm was sabotaged. The glove suggests the culprit is someone who works with electronics.

dialogues.question: Why was there a gap in the log?
dialogues.answer: I was making rounds. I didn't think to log it. But someone must have disabled the alarm during that window.

dialogues.question: Your shoes match the footprint. Explain.
dialogues.answer: I stepped outside for air during the storm. I didn't want to admit it because I wasn't supposed to leave my post.

finalLogic.motive: Dr. Aris Thorne was desperate for money to pay off gambling debts and planned to sell the diamond.
finalLogic.method: He used his knowledge of the observatory to cut the alarm wire during a thunderstorm, used a glass cutter to break the case, and took the diamond. He left a muddy footprint but covered his tracks by blaming Dr. Voss. The burnt wire and glove are key evidence linking him to the sabotage.
finalLogic.winEnding: You present the burnt wire and glove to Dr. Aris, who confesses. The diamond is recovered from his office safe.
finalLogic.failEnding: Without enough evidence, the case goes cold. The diamond is never found.
